first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation down 6% QoQ, directly matching the conditions where memory_31 and memory_86 showed durable gains from signup/onboarding simplification with no noted retention harm. This is a more defensible lever than promotional_pricing: memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing, while attractive against competitor entry pricing, materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a growth strategy—chasing the competitor's price move risks trading long-term qualified revenue for short-term acquisition. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is also relevant but onboarding is further upstream and addresses both declining metrics simultaneously, making it the higher-leverage single experiment. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) don't address the acute SMB-facing declines this week. I verified the two onboarding-related memories since they jointly justify the chosen action and I want to confirm the original effect sizes and whether any retention caveats were omitted in consolidation before committing scarce experiment capacity. Running as a standard (not broad) experiment preserves ability to check for hidden tradeoffs, especially given competitor pricing pressure could confound results.

final.rationale: Verified source records confirm both onboarding-related memories: exp_31 (signup simplification, SMB) shows activation +9%, qualified revenue +4%, with only a small -1% 30-day retention dip, and exp_86 (shortened onboarding) shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved, and retention +3%. Together these directly target this week's observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) without the retention destruction seen in promotional pricing (memory_73), which remains the wrong lever despite competitor pricing pressure since it trades long-term qualified revenue for short-term acquisition. Note exp_31's conclusion explicitly states it holds for SMB but is not replicated in other segments, so I'm scoping this experiment to SMB self-serve accounts rather than broad rollout, and flagging the residual downstream risk (slight retention dip in exp_31, unconfirmed generalization) rather than treating this as a fully de-risked lever. Running as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves the ability to monitor retention and qualified revenue jointly before scaling further, and keeps optionality open for activation_messaging or enterprise_sales_assist as follow-up levers next cycle.
